findings.title: Unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe looks up TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and immediately calls tu.notification_level. If the user has no topic_users row for that topic, tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError. The action should handle the missing record or use TopicUser.change, which creates the row when needed.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed via GET
findings.body: The /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe route is a GET route and TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately mutates TopicUser.notification_level. GET requests are not protected by Rails CSRF tokens and can be triggered by link prefetching, email-client previews, or embedded resources while a user is logged in. Repeated GETs also move regular users to muted. Use a POST/PUT action with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation before changing state.

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change and loses notification-change side effects
findings.body: The action updates TopicUser with tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the normal path for notification-level changes; it sets notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and publishes the MessageBus notification_level_change event. Bypassing it can leave client state stale and loses notification-change metadata.

findings.title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id for non-User arguments
findings.body: TopicUser.track_visit! assigns user_id as user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic. Callers such as TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic pass integer user ids, so the fallback uses the topic argument as the user id. This creates or updates topic_users rows for the wrong user and corrupts per-user topic state. The fallback should be the user argument.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every use
findings.body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation was changed to include %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder appends this translation whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any existing or plugin caller that enables add_unsubscribe_link but does not supply unsubscribe_url will fail interpolation or emit a broken link. Make the topic-specific line conditional on unsubscribe_url being present or update all callers.

findings.title: Topic title is rendered unescaped with triple braces
findings.body: The template renders {{{stopNotificiationsText}}}, and that property interpolates model.fancyTitle into an HTML string. Triple braces bypass Handlebars escaping, so any HTML in the topic title, or in a future representation of fancyTitle, would be injected into the page. Escape the title or render it through a safe component.

findings.title: No meaningful coverage for the new unsubscribe behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a state-changing unsubscribe endpoint and a new required unsubscribe_url interpolation, but the only spec change merely passes unsubscribe_url to Email::MessageBuilder and still only asserts the global preferences URL. There are no controller/request specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe, including missing TopicUser rows, notification-level transitions, slug redirects, or HTML/JSON behavior, and no spec asserting that the topic unsubscribe URL appears in email bodies or HTML.
